name: Palumata
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct, essentially unattested (Buru area); sole Glottolog ref is an ISO 639-3 registration document.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. 1991. The Buru language of Eastern Indonesia. PhD thesis, Australian National University (hdl 1885/10925).
sources.note: p.28 (sec. 4.1): 'Along the west coast was a language or dialect chain spoken in the former districts of Bara, Hukumina, Tomahu, and Palamata'; footnote cites Hendriks (1897:1) listing Hukumina as spoken in 'Hukumina, Palumata en Tomahu'. Hukumina 'stress patterns and intonation contours are strikingly different from Buru, Kayeli..' -- no location; nothing specific to Palumata. Phonology chapter (5.2) covers Buru stress only.
Nothing. Classification 'Unattested'; AES 'extinct'; 'Retired in ISO 639-3: Duplicate of [huw] Hukumina' (2016-01-15, CR 2015-040); alt names Balamata, Palamata; 0 descriptive references.

Nothing. Two-sentence stub: 'Palumata is an extinct and unattested language. It is believed to have been very closely related to the Austronesian language Hukumina, and perhaps a dialect of it.' Cites Ethnologue 12th ed. (1992) and Karenisa 2024.

sources.citation: Karenisa, Kity. 2024. 'Bahasa Punah di Maluku'. Kantor Bahasa Provinsi Maluku (Kemdikbud), April 2024. Online.
sources.note: Nothing (0 hits for 'tekanan'/'fonologi'). Administrative article: Badan Bahasa's 2016/2017/2019 lists count 'bahasa Palumata' among Maluku's extinct languages; then states 'Bahasa Hukumina dan bahasa Palumata merupakan bahasa yang sama dan masih ada penuturnya' (Hukumina and Palumata are the same language and still have speakers) and drops both from the 2022 extinct list. Live host unresolvable; archived copy (Internet Archive, 11 Jul 2024).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (Editor Ethnologue, SIL). 2015. Change Request 2015-040: retire [pmc] Palumata as a duplicate of [huw] Hukumina (adopted 2016-01-15).
sources.note: Nothing. Rationale p.2: 'Grimes (1995: 3) indicates that Palumata (now extinct) was a dialect of Hukumina (also extinct). He lists alternate names for Palumata as Palamata, Balamata, and Pala Mada.. Hammarstrom (2015) cites Grimes 2000 as his source for Palumata as being counted as Hukumina [huw]'. Sources listed: Grimes 2000, Grimes 1995, Hammarstrom 2015. (SIL site timed out; archived copy (Internet Archive, 23 Jan 2025).)

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. 2000. Defining speech communities on Buru Island: a look at both linguistic and non-linguistic factors. In C.E. Grimes (ed.), Spices from the East: papers in languages of eastern Indonesia, 73-103. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 503.
sources.note: Sec. 7.4.3.1 'Palumata (Palamata, Balamata)', p.99: one paragraph of ethnohistory only -- extinct, spoken in north-west Buru, area now Butonese; 'My assumption at this point is that Palumata and Hukumina were varieties of the same language.' No linguistic data at all; the Hukumina paragraph (7.4.3, p.99) says Hukumina is 'very distinct from Buru in intonation, lexicon and sound correspondences' but gives no stress location.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. 1995. Digging for the roots of language death in eastern Indonesia: the cases of Kayeli and Hukumina. Paper, 69th LSA Annual Meeting, New Orleans. ERIC ED384231.
sources.note: Table p.3 lists 'Palumata (Palamata, Balamata, Pala Mada)' as an extinct dialect under HUKUMINA (Bambaa), alongside Bara and Hukumina; no Palumata data anywhere in the paper. Stress is discussed only for Kayeli and Buru (penultimate on the root); nothing for Hukumina or Palumata.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. 2009. Digging for the roots of language death in eastern Indonesia: the cases of Kayeli and Hukumina. In Margaret Florey (ed.), Endangered Languages of Austronesia, 73-89. Oxford: OUP.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Published version of the 1995 LSA paper (read); might add a line on the Hukumina/Palumata relationship, but the precursor has no Palumata data and no Hukumina stress statement, so superseding content is unlikely.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. 1989. Hukumina (Bambaa) field notes and recordings, Masarete/Kayeli, Buru, May 1989 (unpublished).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only first-hand Hukumina data in existence (one elderly speaker); if Palumata is a variety of Hukumina these notes are the only place a stress pattern for the language could ever be recovered. Grimes himself calls the data too sparse for reliable analysis.

sources.citation: Hendriks, H. 1897. Het Burusch van Masarete. 's-Gravenhage: Martinus Nijhoff.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only pre-modern source naming Palumata; per Grimes it merely lists the Hukumina 'dialect' as spoken in Hukumina, Palumata and Tomahu with no further details, so it is very unlikely to contain Palumata stress data, but it is the last unopened primary. Its phonology section describes Masarete Buru, not Palumata.
